questions.question: 12 men can complete a painting work in 8 days. However, 16 women can complete the same painting work in 12 days. 8 men started painting the house. After 6 days of painting, 2 men were replaced by 4 women. Now how many days will they take to complete the remaining painting?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

12 men can complete a painting work in 8 days.

16 women can complete the same painting work in 12 days

8 men started painting the house.

After 6 days of painting, 2 men were replaced by 4 women

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

12 men can complete a painting work in 8 days = (12 × 8) = 96 

16 women can complete the same painting work in 12 days = (16 × 12) = 192

The ratio of men and women = (96 : 192)

⇒ 1 : 2

Total work = (12 × 1 × 8) = 96 units

Now,

8 men started the painting for 6 days = (8 × 1 × 6) = 48 units

Remaining work = (96 – 48) = 48 units

2 men were replaced by 4 women = (4 × 2) = 8 women

Now,

Time taken to complete the remaining painting = (48/8)

⇒ 6 days

**∴ The required time is 6 days**

questions.question: An almirah was sold at a profit of 15%. If its cost had been 5% less and it had been sold for ₹ 1,470 less, then the profit would have been 10%. What is the cost price of the almirah?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit = 15%

If its cost had been 5% less and it had been sold for ₹ 1,470 less, then the profit would have been 10%. 

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost price of Almirah be x

Then,

SP = x + 15x/100

⇒ (100x + 15x)/100

⇒ 115x/100

⇒ 23x/20

If its cost had been 5% less than CP

⇒ [x – (x × 5/100)]

⇒ (x – 5x/100)

⇒ (100x – 5x)/100

⇒ 95x/100

⇒ 19x/20

And, SP = 23x/20 – 1470

Now,

Profit% = [(23x/20 – 1470) – 19x/20/19x/20]

⇒ (10 × 19x/20 × 1/100) = (4x/20 – 1470)

⇒ (19x/200 – 4x/20) = -1470

⇒ (19x – 40x)/200 = -1470

⇒ -21x/200 = -1470

⇒ x = (1470 × 200)/21

⇒ x = (70 × 200)

⇒ x = Rs. 14,000

**∴ The required Cost price is Rs. 14,000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Let the cost of almirah be x

SP of almirah = (115/100 of x) = 1.15x

CP is 5% less = (95/100 × x) = 0.95x

If its cost had been 5% less and it had been sold for ₹ 1,470 less,

⇒ SP – 1470 = 0.95x

According to the question

Profit% = [(SP – 1470) – 0.95x]/0.95x = 10/100

⇒ [(1.15 – 1470) – 0.95x]/0.95x = 1/10

⇒ 1.15x – 1470 – 0.95x = 0.095x

⇒ 0.2x – 1470 = 0.095x

⇒ (0.2x – 0.095x) = 1470

⇒ 0.105x = 1470

⇒ x = 14000

∴ The required Cost price is Rs. 14,000.

A wire is in the form of a square of side 33 cm. If the wire is molded to form a circle, then what is the radius of the circle? 

(Use pi = {22 over 7})
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a wire is remolded, the total length (perimeter) remains constant.

Circumference of Circle = Perimeter of Square

2 × (22 / 7) × r = 4 × 33

(44 / 7) × r = 132 ⇒ r = 3 × 7 = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the square (a) = 33 cm

π = 22 / 7

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a square = 4 × a

Circumference of a circle = 2 × π × r (where r is the radius)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b90186e50b7eef4f799c922119a5273b552448e8dedb8f9f7e61429e76863ca4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total length of the wire = Perimeter of the square

⇒ Total length of the wire = 4 × 33 = 132 cm

⇒ When the same wire is bent into a circle, Circumference = Total length of the wire

⇒ 2 × π × r = 132

⇒ 2 × (22 / 7) × r = 132

⇒ (44 / 7) × r = 132

⇒ r = (132 × 7) ÷ 44

⇒ r = 3 × 7

⇒ r = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Remolding 2D Shapes

When a wire is bent or reshaped from one 2D figure to another, its total length or boundary perimeter always remains constant.

Area and Perimeter Relation

For a given constant perimeter, a circle always encloses the maximum possible area compared to any other 2D polygon like a square, rectangle or triangle.

Remolding 3D Shapes

Similar to 2D figures, when a solid 3D object is melted and recast into another shape, its total volume remains strictly constant.

questions.question: Two dealers offer an item at the same marked price ₹ 3,000. The first dealer allows successive discounts of 10% and 15%. The other dealer allows successive discounts of 20% and 5%. Find the difference in the selling price of the item under the two offers.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two dealers offer an item at the same marked price = Rs. 3000

The first dealer allows successive discounts = 10% and 15%

The other dealer allows successive discounts = 20% and 5%

**Formula used:**

Successive discount = [x + y – (xy/100)]

**Calculation:**

The first dealer allows successive discounts = 10% and 15%

⇒ [10 + 15 – (10 × 15/100)]

⇒ (25 – 3/2)

⇒ (50 – 3)/2

⇒ 47/2

⇒ 23.5%

The other dealer allows successive discounts = 20% and 5%

⇒ [20 + 5 – (20 × 5)/100]

⇒ (25 – 1)

⇒ 24%

The difference in the selling price of the item under the two offers = Rs. [3000 × (24 – 23.5)/100]

⇒ Rs. (3000 × 0.5/100)

⇒ Rs. (30 × 0.5)

⇒ Rs. 15

**∴ The required difference is Rs. 15**

questions.question: In a joint family of 16 persons, the eldest and the youngest members have an age difference of 82 years. If these two are left out of the counting, then the average age of the remaining 14 persons is 28. The average age of the entire family being 30, what is the age of the eldest person?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The difference of an age of the eldest and youngest members = 82 years

The average age of remaining 14 persons = 28

The average age of the entire family = 30

**Formula used:**

Average = sum of observations/Number of observations

**Calculation:**

Let the age of eldest and youngest be x and y respectively

The difference of an age of the eldest and youngest members = 82 years

⇒ (x – y) = 82 ....(1)

Now,

The average age of remaining 14 persons = (14 × 28) = 392

The average age of the entire family = (16 × 30) = 480

The age of the eldest and youngest family = (480 – 392) = 88

So,

(x + y) = 88 ....(2)

Now,

Adding equation (1) and (2), we get 

⇒ (x – y) = 82 + (x + y) = 88

⇒ 2x = (88 + 82)

⇒ 2x = 170

⇒ x = 85 years

**∴ The age of the eldest person is 85 years**

questions.question: A large container has a 50 litre mixture of juice and water in the ratio 3 ∶ 2. To this, a 60 litre juice and water mixture is added, that has a juice to water ratio of 2 ∶ 1. After this, 11 litres of the solution is replaced with pure juice. What is the ratio of water to juice in the final mixture?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mixture of juice and water = 50 litre

The ratio of juice and water = 3 : 2

A 60 litre juice and water mixture is added, that has a juice to water ratio of 2 ∶ 1

After this, 11 litres of the solution is replaced with pure juice

**Calculation:**

The juice in the mixture = (3/5 × 50) = 30 litre

The water in the mixture = (2/5 × 50) = 20 litre

Now,

A 60 litre juice and water mixture is added, that has a juice to water ratio of 2 ∶ 1

The juice in the mixture = (2/3 × 60) = 40

The water in the mixture = (1/3 × 60) = 20

Now,

Total mixture of juice = (30 + 40) = 70 litre

Total mixture of water = (20 + 20) = 40 litre

The ratio of juice and water = (70 : 40)

⇒ 7 : 4

Now,

The ratio of juice = (70 – 7) = 63 litre

The ratio of water = (40 – 4) = 36 litre

Now,

11 litres of the solution is replaced with pure juice

⇒ (63 + 11) : 36

⇒ 74 : 36

⇒ 37 : 18

The ratio of water to juice in the final mixture = 18 : 37

**∴ The required ratio is 18 : 37**

questions.question: Seats in a college for B.Sc. course for Physics, Chemistry and Biology, are in the proportion of 7 ∶ 5 ∶ 8. There is a proposal to increase the seats by 50%, 40% and 25%, respectively. What will be the proportion of the increased seats?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of Physics Chemistry and Biology = 7 : 5 : 8

Increased percent in Physics = 50%

Increased percent in Chemistry = 40%

Increased percent in Biology = 25%

**Formula used:**

Increased value = Original value × (1 + increased%/100)

**Calculation:**

Let the seats in Physics, Chemistry and Biology be 7x, 5x and 8x respectively.

Number of seats in Physics after increment = (7x × 150/100)

⇒ (7x × 3/2)

⇒ 21x/2

Number of seats in Chemistry after increment = (5x × 140/100)

⇒ (5x × 7/5)

⇒ 7x

Number of seats in Biology after increment = (8x × 125/100)

⇒ (8x × 5/4)

⇒ 10x

Increased ratio = (21x/2 : 7x : 10x)

⇒ 21x : 14x : 20x

⇒ 21 : 14 : 20

**∴ The required ratio is 21 : 14 : 20**

questions.question: A is 30% more efficient than B. If B finishes a work in 13 days, then in how many days will A finish the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A is 30% more efficient than B

Time taken by B to finish the work = 13 days

**Concept used:**

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time when the work done is constant.

**Calculation:**

Ratio of efficiency of A and B = 130 : 100

⇒ 13 : 10

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time when the work done is constant.

⇒ Ratio of time taken by A and B = 10 : 13

Let A takes x days to do the same job

⇒ 10 : 13 : : x : 13

⇒ 10/13 : : x/13

⇒ x = (10/13 × 13)

⇒ x = 10 days

**∴ The time taken by A to finish the job is 10 days**

questions.question: A typist uses a paper of size 32 cm × 20 cm. He leaves a margin of 2 cm each on all the sides. If he leaves a margin of 1 cm only on all the sides, then what is the percentage of the increase in the are available for typing (correct to 2 decimal places)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of the paper = 32 cm 

Breadth of the paper = 20 cm

He leaves a margin on all the sides = 2 cm

**Formula used:**

Area of paper = length × breadth

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0372258f4be92b46d20d43fe1747bf8b0bf68be348ffd2c037577f008ef41390.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6975bc0401e8cfb505a55647768a5f638d17a37f6ae567ce116dc65f12cdee35.png] 

According to the question

He leaves a margin of 2 cm each on all the sides

Length of area of the typing = (32 – 2 – 2) = 28 cm

Breadth of area of typing = (20 – 2 – 2) = 16

Area of the typing, when margin leaves 2 cm = (28 × 16) cm²

⇒ 448 cm²

Now,

If he leaves a margin of 1 cm only on all the sides

Length of area of typing = (32 – 1 – 1) = 30 cm

Breadth of the area of typing = (20 – 1 – 1) = 18 cm

Area of the typing, when margin leaves 1 cm = (30 × 18) cm²

⇒ 540 cm²

Now,

Percentage increase = [(540 – 448)/448 × 100]

⇒ (92/448 × 100)

⇒ (9200/448)

⇒ 20.54%

**∴ The required percentage increase is 20.54%**
